name: python-polylith-bidirectional-project-fff7
instr:
polylith cannot reconcile projects bidirectionally to a desired set of bases. Add dependency-closed planning, safe application for Poetry, PEP 621, and Hatch, and reporting of only the committed composition.

Keep discovery and planning within one workspace, namespace, and project. Validate every requested base before exposing changes. Exclude same-named bricks from elsewhere. Deterministically compare current membership with the transitive component closure of retained target bases. Partition changes into additions, removals, retentions, and blocked removals. Include complete importer evidence ordered by brick identity.

Apply only planned namespace-qualified declarations. Preserve established representations for additions and existing keys and values for retained and blocked mappings. Keep unrelated packages, mappings, project tables, and tool tables byte-equivalent.

Successful application returns actual committed membership after writing. Write failures or mismatches raise `ReconciliationApplyError`, a RuntimeError carrying `expected` and `observed`, without exposing success. Unknown projects raise `CompositionProjectNotFound`, a LookupError carrying `project_name`. Invalid requests raise `InvalidTargetBase`, a ValueError carrying every `invalid_bases` value. `ReconciliationOperation` is a Enum.

`discover_composition(request)`, `plan_reconciliation(request)`, and `apply_reconciliation(plan)` provide discovery, planning, and verified application. `calculate_reconciliation
